checks: root publishes before a blocked deep scan and concurrent SQLite-backed reads remain available
default background preindex discovers unopened children and deep descendants without content GET
refresh TTL avoids repeatedly listing a fresh directory despite repeated local queries
manual targeted refresh applies create/delete/modify atomically and preserves stable sibling identities
errored listings preserve known descendants; only a later successful empty scope removes them
depth limits hold while manual recursive refresh crosses its subtree once and does not follow future children
process restart reuses persisted SQLite metadata while the service is offline
atomic legacy migration retains receipts/pins/events and SQLite stays authoritative after legacy JSON corruption
backend binding changes and unsafe refresh paths fail closed without reusing another scope
10,100-row folder queries use the parent index despite an unrelated corrupt Record; SQL/RPC and JSON timings have no hard speed threshold

folder_queries.method: Warm actual SQLite child query plus Item JSON decoding versus json.loads of retained legacy bytes plus parent filtering; actual provider socket RPC measured separately. These are local fixture measurements, not a before/after Rust benchmark.

path_format.binary: repository-relative when inside the repository; otherwise absolute
path_format.index_database: relative to the removed temporary fixture root

scope: synthetic loopback WebDAV, temporary SQLite/legacy state, deterministic 10,100-row comparison; no real storage
